questions.prompt: Using Astra's personal favorites, explain how a product sentence leads to a data model: why a member-page relationship rather than a boolean on Page, what the composite key and the foreign keys each guarantee, which rule they cannot establish on their own, and what the course's default policy does with favorites when a page is soft-deleted, read, or restored.

keyPoints.text: "A page is a favorite" suggests a boolean; "a member favorites a page" suggests a relationship, and only the second supports independent per-user preferences.
keyPoints.quote: Neither structure is universally correct; the second supports independent user preferences.

keyPoints.text: The favorite is a membership identified by (MemberId, PageId).
keyPoints.quote: propose a membership identified by `(MemberId, PageId)`

keyPoints.text: A composite key or unique constraint prevents duplicate favorites even when two requests race.
keyPoints.quote: A composite key or unique constraint prevents duplicate favorites even if two requests race.

keyPoints.text: Foreign keys prevent relationships to missing members or pages.
keyPoints.quote: Foreign keys prevent relationships to missing members/pages.

keyPoints.text: The service must still check both belong to the allowed workspace and the caller can read the page; two separate foreign keys do not establish that cross-entity rule.
keyPoints.quote: two separate foreign keys do not establish this cross-entity rule by themselves.

keyPoints.text: Default policy: keep favorites across soft delete, hide unreadable or trashed pages on reads, and show them again after restore only if access is still allowed.
keyPoints.quote: retain favorites across soft delete, hide unreadable/trashed pages on reads, and show retained favorites after restore only when access is still allowed.

questions.prompt: Explain how Astra replaces the old Page.IsFavorite boolean with the new relationship: the staged order of the migration, what the old data can and cannot tell you, the default backfill and its trade-off (including private pages), what a migration must not do to decide access, and why a green EnsureCreated database or the existing migration guard is not enough evidence for the upgrade.

keyPoints.text: First add the new relationship and migration while old reads keep working.
keyPoints.quote: Add the new relationship and migration while keeping old reads operational.

keyPoints.text: Then switch writes and every caller-visible projection, verify fresh-database and upgrade paths (idempotent seed included), and only later remove the obsolete boolean.
keyPoints.quote: Remove the obsolete boolean in a later migration once the transition is complete.

keyPoints.text: The old boolean carries no information about who clicked it.
keyPoints.quote: The old boolean contains no information about who clicked it.

keyPoints.text: Default backfill: one relationship for each current member who can read each historically starred page.
keyPoints.quote: seed a relationship for each current member who can read each historically starred page.

keyPoints.text: That keeps visible stars for current readers but does not reconstruct historical intent, and the trade-off goes in an ADR.
keyPoints.quote: This preserves visible stars for current readers but does not reconstruct historical intent. State that trade-off in an ADR.

keyPoints.text: Private pages are Owners-only, so inaccessible pages are not backfilled for other roles.
keyPoints.quote: do not backfill inaccessible pages for other roles.

keyPoints.text: SQL migrations must not call a running API to decide access.
keyPoints.quote: Do not make SQL migrations call a running API to decide access.

keyPoints.text: EnsureCreated bypasses migration history and the guard only checks model/snapshot agreement, so a real old-data upgrade fixture is still needed.
keyPoints.quote: a real old-data upgrade fixture is still needed for backfill semantics.

questions.prompt: Distinguish authentication from authorization in Folio and say where the member id must come from. Then explain why "all writes require Editor" is wrong for this app, why both direct and indirect surfaces need permission tests and a hidden button is not protection, and, for concurrency, what a transaction, a unique key, an exists-check and an optimistic concurrency token each do or fail to do.

keyPoints.text: Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization decides whether that caller may do this action on this resource.
keyPoints.quote: Authorization decides whether that caller can perform this action on this resource.

keyPoints.text: The member id comes from server-resolved claims, not a memberId supplied in the request.
keyPoints.quote: should come from server-resolved claims, not an arbitrary `memberId` supplied in a favorite request.

keyPoints.text: Comments and favorites are allowed with read access, so "all writes require Editor" is an incorrect simplification.
keyPoints.quote: "All writes require Editor" would therefore be an incorrect simplification for this application.

keyPoints.text: Indirect surfaces such as tree, search, quick-open, backlinks, export and notifications can all reveal information, so test them as well as page detail.
keyPoints.quote: Use both direct and indirect tests

keyPoints.text: Hiding an edit button cannot stop a forged HTTP request.
keyPoints.quote: A hidden edit button is a helpful cue but cannot stop a forged HTTP request.

keyPoints.text: A transaction commits or rolls back a set of database operations together but does not include an external network call.
keyPoints.quote: It does not automatically include an external network call.

keyPoints.text: A unique key protects an invariant against competing inserts, while an application-side exists-check alone can race.
keyPoints.quote: An application-side "exists?" check alone can race.

keyPoints.text: An optimistic concurrency token protects overlapping writers only if it is part of the actual conditional write; an in-memory comparison covers only what it observes.
keyPoints.quote: An optimistic concurrency token must be part of the actual conditional write or equivalent database protection to cover overlapping writers
